note: Known ways Playwright's engine builds differ from the browsers people use. compare_engines.py marks a candidate with an entry's id when one of its engines is the entry's engine, the capture platform is one of the entry's platforms (or wasn't recorded), its subkind is listed, and the regex matches its image source, element, detail or messages. A marked candidate has low confidence and goes to needs_review until a real browser confirms it. platforms are Python sys.platform values (win32, linux, darwin); null means every platform.

limitations.what: Playwright's WebKit build for Windows decodes no AVIF images: they load but have no pixels or natural size.
limitations.real_browser: Safari decodes AVIF from 16.4 on macOS 13 and later, and on iOS 16 and later (web-features avif: safari 16.4, safari_ios 16.1). Older Safari doesn't, so a page with AVIF and no fallback is still worth a feature finding.
limitations.source: Observed by this skill on a real static site with Playwright WebKit on Windows 11 (2026-11): every AVIF image undecoded, WebP and JPEG fine.
limitations.confirm: Open the page in Safari on macOS or iOS (or Playwright WebKit on macOS) and check the images render.

limitations.what: Playwright's WebKit build for Windows draws text whose font family is the engine default (form controls that don't inherit the page font, placeholders) in a Windows default face: a serif (Times New Roman) or MS Shell Dlg, depending on the machine.
limitations.real_browser: Safari draws form controls in the system font (-apple-system). The page still relies on each engine's default for those controls, so set font: inherit on them whatever the build does.
limitations.source: Observed by this skill on a generated HTML report with Playwright WebKit on Windows 11 (2026-11): filter buttons and a search input in a serif face, Chromium and Firefox in the page's sans-serif.
limitations.confirm: Open the page in Safari on macOS or iOS (or Playwright WebKit on macOS) and compare the controls' font with the page text.

limitations.what: Windows ships no flag emoji glyphs: Chromium and WebKit draw a flag (a pair of regional-indicator letters) as two letters, while Firefox draws it from its bundled colour emoji font. Ink and box differences of flag text are the platform's emoji font, not the page.
limitations.real_browser: Chrome and Edge on Windows also show letters; Safari on macOS and iOS and browsers on Android draw flags. A page that relies on flag emoji to convey something is worth a review either way.
limitations.source: Observed by this skill on a server-rendered site with Playwright Chromium, Firefox and WebKit on Windows 11 (2026-11): flag emoji in a heading and a dropdown drew as letters in Chromium and WebKit, as colour flags in Firefox.
limitations.confirm: Open the page on macOS, iOS or Android and check the flags render, then decide whether letters on Windows are acceptable.

limitations.what: Playwright's Chromium is an open-source build without proprietary codecs (H.264, AAC, HEVC), so MP4 video and AAC audio may not play in it.
limitations.real_browser: Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge include these codecs.
limitations.source: Playwright documentation, Browsers: Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge (media codecs).
limitations.confirm: Rerun capture with the Chrome or Edge channel, or check the page in Chrome.
